1.description: The population balance computes how the floc size distribution changes over time through growth and net aggregation and breakage.
1.quote: eq. 1 describes the time evolution of the floc size distribution.

2.description: The net aggregation rate is the collision-driven formation of flocs of size x minus their loss through further collisions.
2.quote: This model describes both the transport of flocs towards one another ($\beta$) and the probability that these collisions lead to aggregation ($\alpha$) accounting for short-range forces like van der Waals and hydrodynamic interactions.

assumptions.text: The collision efficiency α is taken as a constant between 0 and 1.
assumptions.quote: α was chosen to be a constant between 0 and 1.

2.issue: The aggregation-birth integral uses dx although its integrand and limits are in x′; the differential should be dx′.
review: possible misprint: The aggregation-birth integral uses dx although its integrand and limits are in x′; the differential should be dx′.

3.description: The collision frequency is calculated from the mean velocity gradient and the cube-root size contributions of the colliding flocs.

5.description: The net breakage rate combines the production of size-x flocs from larger flocs with the loss of size-x flocs when they break.
5.issue: The loss term −n(x,t)S(x)Γ(x,x′) contains an unintegrated x′ and applies the daughter distribution to parent disappearance; parent loss should be −n(x,t)S(x).

6.description: The breakage rate increases with floc size according to a power law with coefficient A and exponent a.
6.quote: S(x) is the breakage rate of particles of size x

assumptions.text: The breakage exponent a is fixed at 1/3.

6.issue: Given x is a volume in cm³ and a=1/3, A must have units cm⁻¹s⁻¹ for S to have units s⁻¹, not the stated cm⁻³s⁻¹.
